extracted.intended_audience: NLP/ML researchers and practitioners interested in automated peer review and review evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating NLP systems that generate first-pass peer reviews for scientific papers, and defining/measuring what constitutes a 'good' review.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Good' review (definitional)
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper highlights that 'defining what a "good" review is' is arguably the most difficult part of automating reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the motivating question for the work; implies multiple possible dimensions and that a clear definition is required before automatic review systems can be meaningfully evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation measures for reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors 'first discuss possible evaluation measures for such reviews' (i.e., measures to evaluate automatically generated peer reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper positions explicit evaluation metrics as a necessary component of assessing generated reviews, though the abstract does not list the specific measures; the dataset/experiments are organized around these evaluation considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspects of content covered in each review
rubrics_metrics.description: They 'collect a dataset of papers in the machine learning domain, annotate them with different aspects of content covered in each review'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats review quality partly as which topical/aspectual elements of a paper are discussed (e.g., motivation, methods, experiments, limitations); the presence/absence and treatment of these aspects are used as annotation/evaluation dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage breadth — touching upon aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: System-generated reviews 'tend to touch upon more aspects of the paper than human-written reviews.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage/breadth (number of aspects mentioned) is an evaluative axis — more aspects covered may be a measurable property, but must be weighed against other qualities like constructiveness and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated text can suffer from 'lower constructiveness for all aspects' compared to human reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructiveness (helpfulness, specificity, actionable feedback) is a core quality criterion; systems may mention aspects but provide less useful, concrete, or actionable guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of core ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated reviews are relatively stronger at 'explanation of the core ideas of the papers'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to accurately summarize and explain the main contributions/ideas is a separate evaluative dimension; according to the paper this tends to be handled reasonably well by models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual correctness (of explanations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper notes that explanations of core ideas in generated reviews 'are largely factually correct.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual accuracy of summaries/explanations is explicitly identified as an important metric — correctness about a paper's claims and content is necessary for trustworthy reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility of first-pass reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The work is motivated by producing 'first-pass peer reviews' to assist the human reviewing process and addresses whether such reviews can be of 'high-quality'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied evaluation criterion: usefulness in a real review pipeline (do generated reviews meaningfully reduce human workload or improve review quality?), which must balance breadth, constructiveness, and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research challenges for review generation
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors 'summarize eight challenges in the pursuit of a good review generation system together with potential solutions'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although specifics are not in the abstract, the presence of enumerated challenges implies criteria around robustness, factuality, alignment with review norms, domain knowledge, evaluation difficulty, and system reliability; these are intended to guide future system requirements and evaluation priorities.
